stories.title: 69 killed in high‑speed train crash in central Spain
stories.summary: A collision on the high‑speed rail line south of Madrid resulted in 69 bodies being recovered from wreckage strewn across the tracks and an embankment in central Spain. The crash follows a similar accident near Córdoba nine months earlier. Authorities have opened a formal investigation into the Toledo train disaster.
stories.why: The disaster undermines public confidence in Spain’s rail system and comes weeks before a snap general election.
stories.change: New high-signal event entered the brief.

stories.title: Hundreds Evacuated from Russian‑Occupied Oleshky During Humanitarian Ceasefire
stories.summary: On Friday, hundreds of residents of Oleshky, a city under Russian occupation, were evacuated during a four‑hour humanitarian ceasefire that the BBC reports was brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. The evacuation took place despite ongoing shortages of electricity and water, and some residents chose to remain in the city.
stories.why: The evacuation underscores the severe humanitarian challenges in occupied zones and demonstrates how ceasefire agreements can create brief windows for civilian safety.
stories.previousTitle: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare Ukraine ceasefire
stories.previousSummary: Hundreds of residents of the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have been evacuated, Russian and Ukrainian authorities have said, following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Ukrainian authorities confirmed the evacuees were on their way to southern Russia, from where they will travel on to Ukraine through Belarus.

stories.title: New India slips into red with 1,267 cr loss in Q2
stories.summary: New India Assurance Company has revealed a concerning net loss of ₹1,267 crore for the September quarter, sharply contrasting with last year's profit of ₹63 crore. Despite this, gross written premiums showed a modest increase of 5.14% year-on-year, totaling ₹11,083 crore.
stories.why: This can affect market expectations, company valuations, sector sentiment or capital flows.

stories.title: Spain transport minister says he will not resign after high‑speed rail crash
stories.summary: Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente told a Madrid news conference that he will not resign following the high‑speed rail collision that killed at least 69 people. He said he has “nothing to hide” and that his priority is to resolve the problem rather than discuss his position. He acknowledged ongoing calls for his resignation from political opponents, a trade union and protesters who demonstrated outside the ministry.
stories.why: It indicates how the government is handling political accountability while addressing the emergency response to a major transport disaster.

stories.title: India's services trade surplus rises to $53.39 billion in Q2
stories.summary: The country received $113.029 billion under this head during the three months while it paid $59.637 billion, the data showed. September saw the biggest surplus at $19.208 billion while it was $17.647 billion and $16.537 billion in July and August respectively.
stories.why: This matters because it can affect economic growth, prices, employment, borrowing costs or trade decisions.

stories.title: Nvidia in talks to co‑sign debt for Nscale’s West Virginia AI data center
stories.summary: Nvidia is discussing a residual‑value guarantee that would co‑sign billions of dollars in debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia. Under the proposal, Nvidia would step in if Nscale defaults on construction payments, temporarily take over the facility and help find a buyer or new tenant. Anthropic has signed a $44.6 billion contract for the first 460‑MW building, and a second deal of roughly $45 billion is also being discussed.
stories.why: It indicates Nvidia’s willingness to directly back AI infrastructure financing amid growing investor concerns about the cost of AI data‑center expansion.

stories.title: RBI discusses economic risks at 625th Central Board meeting
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India convened its 625th Central Board meeting, chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra, during which board members deliberated a range of economic risks facing the country. The Economic Times reported that the discussion centered on assessing macro‑economic challenges that could impact financial stability and credit conditions.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: India PE/VC investments jump 45% to $7 billion in September, highest in over two years
stories.summary: Private equity and venture capital investments in India saw significant growth in September 2026. Large-value deals accounted for 76% of the total investments during the July-September quarter.
stories.why: This matters because it could affect India’s economy, major industries, investment, jobs or trade.
